examples.en: I received a gold ring as a gift.
I painted the box a pretty gold color.
The river shines like gold in the evening sunlight.
Gold is flashy, so it suits a party.
My watch is gold, not silver.

examples.ko: 금색과 검은색이 섞인 옷이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like clothes that mix gold and black.

explain: '금색'은 색 이름이고 '금'은 물질 이름이에요. '은색'과 '은'도 같은 짝이에요. 금색 물건은 '금색 반지'처럼 앞에 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: 금색 is the color name and 금 is the metal itself. 은색 and 은 work the same way. Put 금색 before a noun to describe a gold-colored object, as in 금색 반지.

en: to do labor; to toil (manual work)

examples.en: My father does labor in a factory.
I worked eight hours a day.
People who labor need days off.
After physical work, the meal tastes great.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 노동할 수밖에 없었던 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people had no choice but to work from a young age.
I'm tired from working since early morning.

explain: '노동하다'는 몸이나 힘을 써서 일하고 돈을 번다는 느낌이 있어요. 평소 대화에서는 '일하다'를 더 많이 써요. '노동자', '노동 시간' 같은 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 노동하다 carries the feel of working with body or strength to earn a living. In everyday talk 일하다 is used far more often. It is useful to learn it together with words like 노동자 (worker) and 노동 시간 (working hours).

p.n: 노동하다 stresses labor, usually manual, and sounds heavy or social. 일하다 is neutral.

examples.ko: 구청에서 노점 단속을 강화하자 상인들이 반발했어요.
examples.en: When the district office stepped up its crackdown on street stalls, the vendors pushed back.
I bought hotteok from a street stall on my way home from work.
Street stalls line up in front of the market.
The woman at the street stall gave me extra tangerines.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 노점이 문을 안 열어요.
examples.en: On rainy days the street stalls don't open.
Grandmother sells wild greens at a street stall.

explain: 길가에 건물 없이 물건을 놓고 파는 가게예요. 장사하는 사람은 '노점상'이라고 하고, 천막을 치고 음식과 술을 파는 곳은 '포장마차'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 단속이나 상권 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a stall selling goods at the roadside without a building. The seller is a '노점상', and a tent stall selling food and drinks is a '포장마차'. In the news it often appears in stories about crackdowns or shopping districts.

examples.en: The two people's opinions are completely opposite.
The result was the opposite of what I first expected.

examples.ko: 형과 저는 성격이 서로 반대돼서 자주 싸워요.
examples.en: My brother and I have opposite personalities, so we fight often.

examples.ko: 서로 반대되는 단어를 같이 외우면 쉬워요.
examples.en: It's easier if you memorize opposite words together.

examples.ko: 그 방법은 학교 규칙과 반대될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: That method might go against the school rules.

examples.ko: 두 그림은 색이 반대되고 모양은 같아요.
examples.en: The two pictures have opposite colors and the same shape.

explain: '반대하다'는 사람이 '싫어요'라고 하는 행동이고, '반대되다'는 두 가지가 서로 정반대인 관계예요. 그래서 '반대되는 말', '반대되는 의견'처럼 명사 앞에서 자주 나와요. 어떤 계획을 막으려는 상황이면 '반대하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 반대하다 is an action where a person says no. 반대되다 describes two things standing in direct contrast, so it often appears before nouns, as in 반대되는 말 or 반대되는 의견. If someone is trying to block a plan, use 반대하다.

examples.en: New Zealand is an island country.
An island nation is surrounded by the sea.

examples.ko: 저는 작은 섬나라로 여행을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to travel to a small island country.
In this island country people often eat fish.
Britain is also an island nation, and the weather is often cloudy.
Korea is not an island country; it is on a peninsula.

explain: '섬나라'는 한 단어라서 띄어 쓰지 않아요. 영국이나 뉴질랜드처럼 섬으로 이루어진 나라를 이렇게 불러요. 한국은 대륙에 이어진 '반도'에 있는 나라라서 섬나라가 아니에요.
explain_en: 섬나라 is one word, so you do not put a space in it. Countries made of islands, like Britain or New Zealand, are called this. Korea sits on a 반도 (peninsula) connected to the continent, so it is not a 섬나라.

examples.en: People these days consume a lot of goods.

examples.ko: 이 차는 기름을 적게 소비해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This car is popular because it uses little fuel.

examples.ko: 한 달에 얼마나 소비하는지 적어 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote down how much I spend a month.
Let's try to cut down on things that use energy.
I used up too much time.
I try not to spend wastefully.

explain: '소비하다'는 돈, 물건, 에너지, 시간을 써서 없애는 것을 두루 말해요. '쓰다'가 일상어라면 '소비하다'는 경제나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요. '소비자', '소비 생활'처럼 명사와 합친 말이 많아요.
explain_en: 소비하다 covers using up money, goods, energy or time. 쓰다 is the everyday word, while 소비하다 appears more in economics and news. It also forms many compounds such as 소비자 (consumer).

examples.en: This place's soft tofu stew is a little spicy.
I add an egg to the soft tofu stew and eat it.
Soft tofu is gentle and easy to eat.
I bought soft tofu and made a stew.

examples.ko: 간장을 살짝 넣어서 순두부를 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes good to eat soft tofu with a little soy sauce.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 순두부가 아주 부드럽고 고소해요.
examples.en: The soft tofu at this restaurant is very smooth and nutty.

explain: 보통 두부는 눌러서 굳히지만, 순두부는 굳히기 전이라 몽글몽글하고 부드러워요. 그래서 찌개로 많이 끓여 먹어요.
explain_en: Regular tofu is pressed to firm up, but 순두부 is not yet pressed, so it is soft and curdy. That is why it is often cooked into stew.

en: to be useless; to be unworthy; to be unusable

examples.en: This box is useless now.
That book was useless to me.
It seems useless, but let's take it anyway.
I threw away a lot of useless things.
This key is old, useless, and heavy.
The old information was useless, so I deleted it.

explain: 사람에게 '쓸모없다'라고 하면 아주 심한 말이 돼요. 반대말은 '쓸모 있다'이고, '쓸모가 없다'로 띄어 말하기도 해요. '필요 없다'는 지금 필요하지 않다는 느낌이고, '쓸모없다'는 쓰임이 아예 없다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Saying '쓸모없다' about a person is very harsh. The opposite is '쓸모 있다', and you can split it as '쓸모가 없다'. '필요 없다' means not needed right now, while '쓸모없다' means having no use at all.

examples.en: My younger sibling is left-handed.

examples.ko: 왼손잡이는 가위를 쓰기 불편할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Left-handed people sometimes find scissors awkward to use.
I bought a mouse for left-handed people.
I'm left-handed, so I write with my left hand.
There are families with many left-handed people.

examples.ko: 왼손잡이도 오른손을 잘 쓰는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some left-handed people also use their right hand well.

explain: 오른손잡이의 짝말이에요. 두 손을 다 잘 쓰는 사람은 '양손잡이'라고 해요. 도구를 살 때는 '왼손용'이라고 적힌 표시를 확인하면 돼요.
explain_en: It is the counterpart of '오른손잡이' (right-hander). Someone who uses both hands well is '양손잡이'. When buying tools, check for a label saying '왼손용' (for left hand).

examples.en: This company distributes fruit nationwide.

examples.ko: 신선한 채소를 빨리 유통하는 방법이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need a way to distribute fresh vegetables quickly.
Distributing goods online lowers costs.
Some farmers also distribute rice themselves.
They inspect the quality before sending it out to supermarkets.

examples.ko: 가짜 상품을 유통한 가게가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The shop that circulated fake goods closed down.

explain: 만든 사람의 손을 떠난 물건이 도매상과 가게를 거쳐 소비자에게 가는 과정에 써요. '배달하다'는 물건을 가져다주는 일이고, '유통하다'는 그 전체 과정을 말해요. 식품 포장에 '유통 기한'이라는 말이 있어요.
explain_en: It covers goods moving from the maker through wholesalers and shops to consumers. '배달하다' is bringing an item to someone, while '유통하다' is the whole process. Food packaging carries the term '유통 기한'.

dis.h: sell goods through distribution channels; actor

p.n: 유통되다 is passive and cannot take an object.

examples.ko: 중고품 가게에서 안 쓰는 물건을 사 줘요.
examples.en: The secondhand shop buys items you no longer use.

examples.ko: 중고품은 값이 싸지만 상태를 꼭 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Secondhand items are cheap, but you must check their condition.
I buy and sell secondhand items through an app.
This desk is secondhand, but it's as clean as new.

examples.ko: 중고품 거래할 때는 직접 만나서 확인하세요.
examples.en: When trading secondhand items, meet in person to check.
I sold the furniture I wasn't using as secondhand goods.

explain: '중고차', '중고책'처럼 '중고'는 이미 한 번 쓴 물건을 뜻하고, 반대는 '새 제품'이에요. '중고'가 중학교·고등학교의 '중고'와 소리가 같으니 문장 속에서 구별하세요.
explain_en: As in '중고차' and '중고책', '중고' means something that has already been used once, and the opposite is '새 제품'. It sounds the same as the '중고' in middle and high school, so tell them apart by context.

en: to advance into; to enter (a field or market)

examples.en: Our company is entering overseas markets.
The Korean team advanced to the finals.
That singer will break into the US market.
I want to make my way into the film industry.
More women are entering the workforce.

examples.ko: 유명한 커피 가게가 우리 동네에 진출했대요.
examples.en: I heard a famous coffee chain has moved into our neighborhood.

explain: '진출하다'는 새로운 곳이나 분야, 다음 단계로 나아갈 때 써요. 스포츠에서는 '결승에 진출하다'처럼 다음 경기로 올라간다는 뜻으로 많이 말해요. '~에 진출하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 진출하다 is used for moving into a new place, field or next stage. In sports it is very common, as in '결승에 진출하다' (to reach the finals). It takes 에, as in '~에 진출하다'.

examples.ko: 새 병원은 최신식 장비를 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: The new hospital is equipped with the latest equipment.
That factory switched to state-of-the-art facilities.
It is a modern building, so the facilities are very clean.

examples.ko: 최신식 주방이 있는 집으로 이사하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move to a house with a modern kitchen.
Our school library is completely up to date.

examples.ko: 최신식이라고 해서 꼭 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being the latest does not necessarily mean it is good.

explain: 주로 '최신식 장비', '최신식 건물'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 반대말은 '구식'이에요. 휴대폰이나 자동차 같은 제품에는 '최신형'이 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before a noun, as in '최신식 장비' or '최신식 건물'. The opposite is '구식'. For products like phones and cars, '최신형' often sounds more natural.

examples.en: They made the floor of the building from concrete.
We waited a day for the concrete to harden.
There are many concrete buildings in the city.

examples.ko: 콘크리트 길은 비가 와도 흙탕물이 안 생겨요.
examples.en: A concrete road does not get muddy water even when it rains.
Workers poured concrete and built a wall.

examples.ko: 차가운 콘크리트 위에 앉으면 엉덩이가 시려요.
examples.en: If you sit on cold concrete, your bottom gets chilly.

explain: '콘크리트를 붓다', '콘크리트가 굳다'처럼 써요. '시멘트'는 콘크리트를 만드는 가루 재료라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is used as in '콘크리트를 붓다' (pour concrete) and '콘크리트가 굳다' (concrete hardens). '시멘트' is the powder used to make concrete, so the two are different.

en: student on leave of absence; student taking a break from study

examples.ko: 저는 지금 휴학생이라서 낮에 아르바이트를 해요.
examples.en: I'm on leave from school now, so I work part-time during the day.
Can students on leave use the library too?
There are quite a few students on leave in our department.

examples.ko: 휴학생 때 여행도 하고 자격증도 땄어요.
examples.en: While I was on leave, I traveled and got a certificate.
I asked whether students on leave also get the student discount.

examples.ko: 형은 휴학생이어서 집에서 시간을 많이 보내요.
examples.en: My older brother is on leave, so he spends a lot of time at home.

explain: 학교로 돌아오면 '복학하다', 돌아온 학생은 '복학생'이라고 불러요. 대학교 이야기에서 아주 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: When a student returns to school it is '복학하다', and that student is called a '복학생'. This word is very common in talk about university life.
